findings.evidence: "`TZ=ZONE python3 "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/claude_digest.py" --date DAY --format json`". The skill covers Windows for the window one-liner ("plus the `tzdata` package on Windows"), but the digest branch relies on a POSIX `TZ=` prefix, and claude_digest.py calls `astimezone()` with no argument. On Windows, Python does not apply an IANA `TZ` value that way, so the digest silently splits days in the system zone instead of ZONE
findings.fix: Add one sentence after the table: "On Windows, a `TZ=` prefix is not applied: run the digest only when the system time zone equals ZONE, otherwise say in one line that session days may be off and confirm the picked sessions with the user."
